label: Christopher C. 'Kit' Green
narrative: Green is the medical end of the reverse-engineering programme, and his released DIRD is one of the most revealing documents in the entire corpus because of what it takes for granted. A physician-neuroscientist who ran life-sciences analysis for CIA's Office of Scientific Intelligence before moving to General Motors and then Wayne State University, Green was the analyst to whom the intelligence community's biological anomalies were routed - including, in the 1970s, the SRI remote-viewing work. His AAWSAP paper, 'Clinical Medical Acute & Subacute Field Effects on Human Dermal & Neurological Tissues', was released publicly by Popular Mechanics on 14 February 2020, and its cover carries the imprint of Puthoff's Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin. Its preface quotes verbatim from a November 2007 proposal addressed 'to Puthoff/Hathaway' which states the intention plainly: 'certain characteristics of the fields associated with exotic propulsion can with near certainty be gleaned from archival records of their effects on human physiology.' Its Hypothesis One is that 'sufficient evidence exists from human injury / effects to reverse engineer certain aspects of the Energy / Propulsion Systems'. Its executive summary concludes that 'some advanced systems are already deployed, and opaque to full US Intelligence understanding'. It contains a Schuessler catalogue appendix, a 'Green-Morris Cases' appendix, and an ICD-diagnostics appendix built on 42 peer-reviewed cases plus roughly 300 unpublished ones, and it names the Cash-Landrum event. This is a US intelligence contractor document that treats humans injured by unidentified craft as an instrumented dataset for reverse engineering exotic propulsion.
